newsitem.title: RUSSIA: China's Jiang to visit Russia, sign border pact.
newsitem.headline: China's Jiang to visit Russia, sign border pact.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin will visit Russia this month to build the foundations for a closer relationship in the 21st century after decades of distrust.

Jiang's trip, which the Kremlin announced would take place from April 22 to 26, will step up Russian efforts to strengthen ties in the East as it faces difficulties in relations with the West over NATO's plans to expand eastwards.

During Jiang's visit he, President Boris Yeltsin and leader the Central Asian states of Tajikistan, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan are due to sign an accord reducing military forces along the former Soviet-Chinese border.

"The visit will be an important stage in the process of filling with real content the new formula of Russia-China relations -- an equal trusted partnership aimed at strategic co-operation in the 21st century," a Kremlin statement said.
Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen visited Moscow last month to prepare for Jiang's arrival but no date for the trip had been announced.
Russia and China formed a strong alliance in the early 1950s but it degenerated into bitter rivalry for leadership of the communist world and led to border clashes in the late 1960s.

Relations have been warming since Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev visited Beijing in 1989. Visits to China by Yeltsin in December 1992 and in April last year continued the improvement in ties and Jiang said last year that relations with Russia had entered a new age.
Visits by Jiang have also helped bring the two countries closer -- he came to Russia in May 1991 and September 1994 and attended World War Two commemorations in Moscow in May 1995.

The border pact between Moscow, Beijing and the three Central Asian states, which were once part of the Soviet Union, will build on an agreement signed a year ago committing the five countries to a set of border confidence-building measures.
No details about the timing or extent of planned troop reductions have been announced. China's ambassador to Moscow has said the terms may be kept secret even after the pact is signed.
Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov will visit Beijing on April 14 to 18 to discuss the military situation in the region and promote Russian arms sales to China, Itar-Tass news agency said.
Tass said he will meet Jiang, Defence Minister Chi Haotian. The Russian minister will also visit Shanghai and Dalian.

Moscow's border disputes with China have largely been resolved, but some deputies in Russia's Far East urged the government on Thursday to reconsider plans that would give China a sliver of Russian land in demarcating the border.
The Kremlin said on Thursday trade turnover between Russia and China rose by 25 percent in 1996, and joint projects had been launched in energy, transport, space and other fields.
Russia views China as a key trading partner and both countries want to upgrade economic ties which have failed to keep pace with the improving political links.
They are working on a plan to increase cross-border trade by setting up a special zone in the north-eastern Chinese city of Suifenhe that would allow free movement for traders.
The two countries are also negotiating over major deals from nuclear power plants to a natural gas pipeline.

Russia has proposed building a pipeline to carry Siberian natural gas to China and is seeking a role in China's huge Three Gorges dam project. It is also keen to sell military and civil aircraft to China.
